cases.input: One business unit trials a technology.
cases.expect: The scoped stage is recorded independently.
cases.violates: Scope and effective interval are explicit.

cases.input: A decision promotes adoption to preferred.
cases.expect: A successor episode records authority and effective time.
cases.violates: Each transition requires authority and decision.

cases.input: Vendor support ends while local use continues.
cases.expect: Support and adoption states remain separate.
cases.violates: Vendor support and local stage remain separate.

cases.input: Preferred status is treated as proof of conformance.
A stage lacks its scheme version.
cases.violates: Stage pins a named scheme and version.

cases.input: Vendor status silently changes local stage.
An adoption episode carries a stage value resolved from a pinned stage scheme version.
cases.expect: The stage resolves through the pinned scheme and no stage value originates in the candidate.
cases.violates: Stage pins a named scheme and version.

cases.input: A stage value is taken from the candidate's own lifecycle list instead of a pinned scheme version.
cases.expect: The stage is rejected; no stage vocabulary is assumed by the candidate.
cases.violates: (added:) No stage value is enumerated in this candidate; stage values resolve only from the pinned stage scheme version.

cases.input: An episode moves from draft to effective to superseded while its stage value is unchanged.
cases.expect: Record lifecycle and stage vocabulary move independently and remain disjoint.
cases.violates: (added:) The record lifecycle and the stage vocabulary are disjoint.

cases.input: A successor episode for one organization, technology and scope starts exactly at the predecessor's end, and an as-of query is issued inside each window.
cases.expect: Each query returns exactly one effective stage.
cases.violates: (added:) For one organization, technology and scope, at most one episode is effective at any instant.

cases.input: Two episodes for the same organization, technology and scope hold overlapping effective intervals.
cases.expect: The second episode is rejected; as-of resolution must be unambiguous.
cases.violates: (added:) For one organization, technology and scope, at most one episode is effective at any instant.

cases.input: An episode's validFrom precedes the time of its authorizing decision.
cases.expect: The episode is rejected; effect never precedes authorization.
cases.violates: Each transition requires authority and decision.

cases.input: An episode's decision reference is dereferenced for audit.
cases.expect: Rationale, authorized occurrence and issued record all resolve.
cases.violates: (added:) A decision reference resolves the rationale, the authorized occurrence and the issued record.

cases.input: An episode's decision reference resolves only an issued record, with no rationale and no occurrence.
cases.expect: The reference is rejected as an incomplete decision triad.
cases.violates: (added:) A reference that resolves only the issued record is incomplete.

cases.input: The organization reference is filled with a plausible but unallocated registry identifier.
cases.expect: The reference is rejected and must remain an explicit unassigned external referent.
cases.violates: Registry allocation is pending and no identifier may be guessed.
